title: Operational resilience bridge: degradable paths & safepoints - postmortem follow-up
summary: Follow-up to the Dec incident where degraded tail-latency caused partial fallbacks for checkout assistant. We aligned on RCA (KV cache eviction pattern + sudden routing change), agreed short-term mitigations (safepoints, throttles, warm pools) and mid-term hygiene (observability, better canaries, SRE runbook). Action items assigned and a tentative pilot scheduled for the dedicated fallback policy next week.
topics: Pilot plan for dedicated fallback pool
action_items: Samir Patel - share narrowed diagnostic logs + link to runtime trace dump - due 2028-01-14
Jenna Cole - produce a config patch for safepoints + throttling policy and sample helm values - due 2028-01-18
Priya Desai - run replay of peak-traffic trace against proposed config, report latency delta - due 2028-01-19
Miguel Ortiz - schedule 1hr pilot kickoff with Atlas SREs and confirm invite list - due 2028-01-13
Leo Martins - enable additional retention for prefix cache metrics for 7 days and provide access - due 2028-01-15
next_steps: kickoff pilot for dedicated fallback policy w/ warm pool (target: 2028-01-20)
redwood to deliver config patch and safety checks for canary runs
customer to run replays and share perf flash report
follow-up bridge call scheduled for 2028-01-25 15:00 UTC
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2028-01-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel, Jenna Cole, Miguel Ortiz (Redwood); Priya Desai, Oliver Brandt, Tanya Wu, Leo Martins (Atlas Retail)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on root cause and fixes; agree short and medium term plan

00:00 - Samir Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. We wanted this bridgecall to close the loop on last month's degradation during the checkout microburst. how are you all doing?
00:18 - Priya Desai: thanks Samir. yeah, still a bit raw but we've gone through initial notes. we saw the same pattern: a KV cache thrashing at around 03:12 UTC and a spike of route fallbacks.
00:32 - Jenna Cole: right, so quick reminder from redwood side — the runtime logged rapid prefix evictions and then the smart-routing shifted traffic to the lower-tier model which increased token latencies and then that cascaded.
00:51 - Oliver Brandt: one thing we keep circling back to is why the fallback rate didn't kick earlier; our alerts are configured but they were noisy and suppressed.
01:05 - Miguel Ortiz: that sounds like alert fatigue; also our canary didn't trigger because the canary traffic used a slightly different prompt set, so it missed the long-tail prompts.
01:22 - Priya Desai: yes, the prompt shapes in prod expose a longer tail. our SRE replay showed that.
01:35 - Samir Patel: ok, good. so core RCA summary: KV cache eviction pattern amplified by an upstream routing update, plus canary mismatch and gap in tracing. any other root facts to add?
01:48 - Tanya Wu: from a compliance angle, we also noticed audit logs for the edge router had truncated entries during the window which made timeline reconstruction harder. we flagged that for our infra team.
02:05 - Jenna Cole: noted, that matches the partial traces we have. one point — some transcribed names in the logs showed as K-V cash instead of KV cache so the parser missed those fields, that was embarrassing.
02:22 - Leo Martins: (laughs) yeah the parser is temperamental.
02:30 - Samir Patel: Alright, moving to mitigations. We grouped these into immediate (hotfix), short-term (1-2 weeks) and mid-term (1-3 months). I'll run through the immediate items.
02:45 - Jenna Cole: immediate: add safepoints around routing changes so traffic isn't switched mid-epoch; add a throttle window for new sessions; increase prefix cache retention by 30s during high variance spikes.
03:01 - Priya Desai: can you explain 'safepoints' — is that a config flag or code change?
03:10 - Jenna Cole: it's a config-first approach. we add a routing-safepoint boolean that gates aggressive route rebalancing for N seconds after a config push. no runtime recompile needed.
03:23 - Priya Desai: sounds good — the less code change the better for us.
03:29 - Samir Patel: short term we'd also recommend adjusting the canary corpus to include longer-tail prompts and adding an automated replay trigger when a new route is added.
03:44 - Oliver Brandt: replay trigger? so that means anytime we deploy a route change the system runs a traffic replay against the new route?
03:51 - Jenna Cole: yeah, a lightweight replay — sample recent traffic for 1 minute at reduced QPS and measure latency and model mismatch. if it fails thresholds we rollback automatically.
04:05 - Priya Desai: that's key. our previous canary was synthetic and missed real-user prompt diversity.
04:16 - Miguel Ortiz: mid-term: visibility — we need better end-to-end tracing for token-level origin and the routing decisions. also stronger KV cache corruption detection (checksums / monotonic TTLs).
04:30 - Priya Desai: about the KV cache: our team saw a TTL reset that made it look like entries were fresh; is that something on your side or ours?
04:40 - Jenna Cole: preliminary logs indicate concurrent eviction + re-insert race when a node rejoined the pool. there's a short window where the TTL can be reset back to default; we'll tighten the lock path and add a monotonic increment on reinsert.
04:56 - Leo Martins: will that require a rolling restart?
05:00 - Jenna Cole: depends — we have a config patch that avoids the reinsert path and buys us time until we ship the lock fix. the patch is non-breaking and can be applied via helm.
05:14 - Priya Desai: great, please provide the helm values.
05:19 - Samir Patel: next up, fallback policies — currently you have model-tier fallback to cheaper variants in the same region. we propose adding a dedicated warm fallback pool for checkout flows with pre-warmed KV prefixes.
05:36 - Oliver Brandt: pre-warmed prefixes how feasible is that? wouldn't that increase cost a lot?
05:44 - Jenna Cole: it increases reserved footprint a bit but reduces user-visible latencies and error surface. Redwood Optimize can suggest optimal pre-warm size based on your 95/99th token distributions.
05:57 - Priya Desai: acceptable if economics look sane. can you run a cost delta for a small warm pool?
06:04 - Samir Patel: noted - that's an action item for us.
06:08 - Tanya Wu: on privacy — if we keep warm pools, ensure prefixes are not storing raw PII and that we rotate keys and masks regularly. also need confirmation on KMS integration.
06:20 - Jenna Cole: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM for encryption at rest; we'll include the KMS details in the security packet.
06:28 - Priya Desai: good.
06:33 - Miguel Ortiz: another visibility gap was the router audit truncation Tanya mentioned. we recommend doubling audit retention for 72 hours during the pilot window.
06:45 - Leo Martins: done — I can set that from our side but we need the log ingestion schema to accept the extra fields.
06:55 - Samir Patel: we'll share the trace format and mapping.
07:01 - Priya Desai: question: did we consider network L7 blips at the cloud edge? some of the timeouts looked like transient upstream wire timeouts.
07:12 - Jenna Cole: yes, our telemetry shows increased connection resets concurrent with the KV eviction spikes — likely backpressure. we should overlay network metrics with KV evictions for correlation.
07:26 - Oliver Brandt: do you have a dashboard we can use?
07:29 - Jenna Cole: we can share a Grafana dashboard link; I'll add the panels — token latency, prefix eviction rate, route fallback rate, connection resets.
07:42 - Priya Desai: excellent.
07:46 - Samir Patel: ok, timeline for deliverables: Jenna will produce a config patch + helm sample by 2028-01-18; Samir will share narrowed logs and the runtime trace; Miguel will schedule the pilot kickoff; customer to commit to a replay and report results.
08:05 - Priya Desai: can we also get a written runbook for the bridgecall steps — i.e., rollback steps and who to call?
08:13 - Miguel Ortiz: yes, we'll author a 1-page runbook stub and attach it to the pilot invite.
08:20 - Tanya Wu: for the runbook please ensure compliance checklist: audit export, KMS rotation confirmation, and data retention note.
08:31 - Samir Patel: will do.
08:34 - (short silence)
08:40 - Oliver Brandt: wanted to raise one more point — our procurement team is asking about SLA credits if we have repeated degradations. Is this an ops legal discussion?
08:51 - Miguel Ortiz: typically that's legal/procurement; we can connect them but for now we focus on remediation.
09:00 - Priya Desai: agreed. we'll take it offline.
09:06 - Jenna Cole: quick nit: some of the traces had mis-labeled model variants in logs, so our rollback automation didn't pick the right candidate. we'll add more robust model-id annotations.
09:20 - Priya Desai: that will help.
09:23 - Samir Patel: okay we're at 30 minutes in — want to open the floor for questions.
09:28 - Leo Martins: are there any planned infra changes on your side that might affect the pilot?
09:34 - Jenna Cole: no major infra pushes; we'll do the patch as a config apply. we won't touch the kernel or runtime.
09:41 - Priya Desai: what about the synthetic canary corpus — can we collaborate on curating the long-tail prompt set?
09:49 - Jenna Cole: absolutely, we'll provision a shared corpus repo and you can drop in anonymized prompt samples.
09:55 - Priya Desai: we'll sanitize and share.
10:01 - Oliver Brandt: timeline check — when is the next sync?
10:05 - Samir Patel: next bridge scheduled 2028-01-25 at 15:00 UTC, that'll be the pilot status review.
10:12 - Miguel Ortiz: action recaps will be posted to the deal thread in CRM.
10:18 - Priya Desai: thanks. any final safety concerns?
10:22 - Tanya Wu: just reiterating KMS and audit retention requirements — we'll sign off once those are in writing.
10:30 - Samir Patel: understoood. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and the patch.
10:38 - (meeting closes)

Notes on transcription quality: there are occasional mis-hearings (K-V cash, model ids truncated) and speaker overlaps. Some timestamps are approximate.
